question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $69u+30v=\text{gcd}(69,30).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}69 & = & 30\cdot 2 & + & 9 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 30 & = & 9\cdot 3 & + & 3 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 9 & = & 3\cdot 3 & + & 0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(69,30)=3.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}9 & =69-30\cdot 2 \\ 3 & =30-9\cdot 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & =30-9\cdot 3 \\  & =30-(69-30\cdot 2)\cdot 3 \\  & =30\cdot 7-69\cdot 3 \\  & =69\cdot (-3)+30\cdot 7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=-3$ and $v=7.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=(-3)+7=4.
$$
